question: Enter in our plant from the Emergency Room to study an 80-year-old patient reporting weight loss and nonspecific central-abdominal discomfort, together with loss of appetite. The diagnostic process that we must develop during your admission will be guided by the following principles EXCEPT:

options.opa: All those tests that can bring light to the process suspected by the doctor covering the widest differential diagnosis from the beginning will be carried out.
options.opb: The healthcare process will be adapted to the individual clinical context of the patient and it will be sought that the latter be a participant in the decisions regarding diagnosis and treatment.
options.opc: It is important to think first of all in the most ordinary way, only later, once the most frequent entities are discarded with certainty, to consider the odd.
options.opd: Some complementary tests may be redundant and may not add value to the diagnostic process, but at the cost of health. Thus, before two complementary tests of similar performance, it will always be decided by the most economical and least risky.
options.ope: It is essential that the doctor does not add new discomforts with the practice of complementary explorations that are not strictly necessary.

analysis: The principles of medical diagnosis emphasize the importance of considering all possible differential diagnoses, involving the patient in decision-making, prioritizing common conditions, avoiding unnecessary tests, and minimizing patient discomfort. However, it is not recommended to prioritize the most ordinary conditions over the less common ones.
